subject: design-technology
title: Just-In-Time and Lean Manufacturing
welcome_lead: Toyota's revolution: make only what you need, when you need it.
meta_desc: A-Level D&T: JIT, lean manufacturing, and the Toyota Production System.

concepts.def: Just-In-Time — parts arrive exactly when needed.
Card-based pull-signalling system in lean production.
Japanese: waste — the 7 wastes of lean.
Cord/light system letting workers stop the line to flag problems.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Toyota Production System, codified by Taiichi Ohno in the 1950s-70s and popularised internationally from the 1980s, underlies lean. Two pillars: JIT and Jidoka (automation with human touch).
Kanban cards (Japanese 'signboard') trigger upstream production only when downstream pulls. Inventory shrinks to a few hours; capital is freed; quality problems surface fast.
Kaizen — continuous small improvements — and the Andon cord (anyone can stop the line) embed quality and improvement in daily work.
